teaching.hint: For one item, how many different sums could a valid partner produce under the value bounds?

solution_outline.decisive_insight: The allowed pair sums form only 22 values, and fixing a sum determines the partner value.
solution_outline.approach: Scan items, keeping frequencies of earlier values. For each new value, query its complement for every power from 1 through 2^21, add those frequencies, then record the new item.
solution_outline.state_and_invariant: Before querying an item, the table contains exactly earlier indices, with their value multiplicities.
solution_outline.correctness: Each unordered pair has one later index. At that step its earlier item is present, and exactly its own sum selects the matching complement query. All possible positive power-of-two sums are covered and only those sums are queried, so every valid pair is counted once and no invalid pair is counted.
solution_outline.complexity: Expected O(22n) time and O(n) auxiliary space; reduce the count modulo the required modulus.
solution_outline.pitfall: Query before recording the current item to prevent pairing an item with itself; zero plus zero is not a power of two.

common_wrong_turns: Query before recording the current item to prevent pairing an item with itself; zero plus zero is not a power of two.
source_fidelity_notes: Made unordered index-pair semantics explicit; retained zeros, positive power definition, sum bound, and modulo.
